_comment: Cached output of prompts/no_show.md — one `claude -p` call per event. --live regenerates this file; offline mode reads it as-is. Every quote is timestamp-attributable to data/incoming/transcript.md.

marketing.headline: The recording link should already know what they care about.
marketing.body: Sara Alvarez (Meridian Software) suggested pointing no-shows to a timestamp for their specific registration interest rather than the full hour — "you mentioned integration challenges when you registered, here's the twelve-minute mark" — way higher engagement than the whole recording. [16:45]

revops.headline: The fastest fix most teams haven't made.
revops.body: Sara Alvarez (Meridian Software) cut internal lead-routing delay from about 18 hours to under 2 hours and saw webinar-sourced opportunity creation rise 41% the following quarter — same leads, same list, just faster handoff. [11:30]

sales.headline: No-shows out-click your attendees more often than you'd think.
sales.body: Daniel Kim (Northwind Analytics) said their no-show follow-up gets a better click-through rate than their attendee follow-up in 6 of the last 8 webinars — no-shows haven't gotten the value yet, so they're hungrier for it. [15:44]

executive.headline: This no-show list is worth more than a rounding error.
executive.body: Daniel Kim (Northwind Analytics) noted repurposed content from a single webinar generates about 2.4x the pipeline-influenced touches of the live session itself — no-shows who never attended live are a real share of that reach. [38:42]

customer_success.headline: Nothing goes out without a human checking it first.
customer_success.body: Sara Alvarez (Meridian Software) was direct about this in Q&A: personalization should only use data a person actually gave consent for, and a human review step matters most "not just for tone but for exactly this kind of judgment call." [57:38]

general.headline: Segmentation alone triples click-through.
general.body: Sara Alvarez (Meridian Software) shared that moving from one blanket post-webinar email to attendee/no-show/speaker segmentation — plus role-based variants — took overall click-through from about 6% to just over 17%, without changing send timing at all. [28:20]

by_industry.saas: Daniel Kim's fourth-layer point applies directly if you're evaluating this as a SaaS buyer: the section worth your six minutes is the integration-and-security piece he flagged as the real blocker at that tier, more than pricing. [26:52]
by_industry.services_it: If you're running this across client accounts at an IT-services or agency shop, Daniel Kim's fourth-layer point ([26:15]) is exactly why we didn't send you one generic recap — which part is worth your time depends on which client this session was actually for.
by_industry.other_commercial: Per Daniel Kim's fourth-layer point ([26:15]), the six minutes worth your time outside pure enterprise software is the time-to-value-and-pricing section he called out as the real objection for buyers at that size. [26:52]
